title: Dispatch: Supply active campaign rules and source ambiguities to DM context (attempt 1)
description:
Dispatch of eshyra-jhpt.3 (attempt 1). Spec and acceptance criteria live on eshyra-jhpt.3 and the epic eshyra-jhpt; read both, including ADR 0020 TRANSITION AMENDMENT A1 on the bead. This bead carries the supervisor's pre-planning only.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.3.1 on branch eshyra-jhpt.3.1, cut from the integration branch eshyra-jhpt (merge 4a9620e), which already contains the completed eshyra-jhpt.1 domain model and eshyra-jhpt.2 storage/seam. Work only inside that worktree.

SCOPE
DM-side context assembly, plus the campaign-position assignment this bead needs (see part 1). NO auditor parity work (.4 — but build the projection so .4 can reuse it verbatim), NO ambiguity dialogue or player prompting (.6), NO precedent inference (.7), NO replay (.8), NO CLI (.5).

PART 1 — YOU MUST FIRST ESTABLISH CAMPAIGN POSITION ASSIGNMENT. THIS IS THE CENTRAL DESIGN TASK.
eshyra-jhpt.2 made campaignPosition REQUIRED on every active-at-position query (listActiveCampaignRulesAtPosition, listActiveRulingsForAmbiguitiesAtPosition, createCampaignRuleReadSeam). Nothing in the repo can currently produce one at turn time:
  - CampaignPosition is { sessionId, turnId, ordinal } (campaign/campaignRules.ts) and its ordinal is the authoritative chronology key.
  - turnId is generated in packages/cli/src/index.ts makeId() as `turn-<base36 timestamp>-<random>` — opaque and NOT ordered.
  - turn_trace is keyed (campaign_id, session_id, turn_id) with no ordinal; only scene_log.seq and campaign_arc.sequence_no are ordinals, and neither is a campaign-wide turn counter.
So this bead owns assigning and persisting the ordinal.
REQUIRED PROPERTY, because eshyra-jhpt.8 depends on it: the SAME turn must always resolve to the SAME position. A disputed turn is rolled back and replayed, and a rule effective "at the start of the disputed turn" only keeps meaning if the replayed turn occupies the identical position. Do not derive the ordinal from COUNT(*) of turn_trace or any other row count — a rollback changes the count and silently shifts every later position.
DESIGN: add migration 0026 with a small table mapping (campaign_id, session_id, turn_id) -> ordinal, monotonically assigned per campaign on first request and IDEMPOTENT thereafter, plus a resolver (suggested `resolveCampaignPosition(db, { campaignId, sessionId, turnId })`) returning a CampaignPosition. Assign at turn start. Test that re-resolving the same turnId returns the identical ordinal, that a rolled-back-and-replayed turn keeps its position, and that ordinals increase across turns and across a session boundary. Highest existing migration after eshyra-jhpt.2 is 0025_campaign_rules.sql, so yours is 0026_*.sql. Never edit an existing migration — migrationRunner.ts checksums applied ones — and update packages/core/test/migrationLegacyAdoption.test.ts ledger expectations, which is mandatory and not a test weakening.

PART 2 — SUPPLY ACTIVE CAMPAIGN RULES TO DM CONTEXT.
packages/core/src/orchestrator/contextAssembler.ts is the DM context builder: ContextAssemblyInput -> assembleContext() -> AssembledContext -> renderContextMessage(). It currently carries no rules slice at all.
- Add a campaign-rules slice to AssembledContext and render it in renderContextMessage.
- At initial scale supply ALL active campaign-rule prose at the current position on every applicable DM turn. Correctness beats selective retrieval; do not add retrieval scoring or a budget heuristic.
- Include stable rule identity, kind, effective provenance, and linked ambiguity/interpretation provenance. Do not ask the model to execute deterministic state logic.
- USE THE eshyra-jhpt.2 QUERIES DIRECTLY. Do not write a second active-rule resolver, do not cache rules in campaign state, and do not copy pack data into campaign state. The exact same projection must be reusable by eshyra-jhpt.4 for the auditor — factor the projection so .4 calls the identical function rather than rebuilding it. This is the whole point of amendment A1 and of transition W11's prohibition on a discovery-local store.
- AMENDMENT A1: the active-rule projection must expose, per rule, the linked ambiguity ID and, where one exists, the governing pack record key, so a consumer can pair a rule with its governing source material without re-deriving the association. CampaignRuleProjection already carries `ambiguityId` and `governingRecordKeys`; confirm both survive into whatever you hand the DM, and test it.

PART 3 — SURFACE UNRESOLVED SOURCE AMBIGUITY WITHOUT INVENTING CERTAINTY.
The shipped pack contains exactly THREE ambiguities (verified by grep over packages/core/data/rules-packs/): ambiguity:create-undead-ghast-wight-composition, ambiguity:find-familiar-permanent-dismissal-after-zero-hp, ambiguity:cube-of-force-same-face-duration-reset. Relevance selection is therefore not a scaling problem at initial scale — surface every unresolved one from the active rules stack and skip retrieval optimization entirely, consistent with the bead's "correctness takes priority over selective retrieval".
- RulesAmbiguity (rules/types.ts) is { id, question, source[], affects[], interpretations[{id, summary}], canonicalResolution: null, runtimeDisposition: { status: 'engine-pending', owner: 'campaign-ruling' } }. canonicalResolution is permanently null and the owner is 'campaign-ruling' — that is the source telling you it has no answer.
- For each ambiguity with NO active ruling at the current position, the rendered context must carry the question, the enumerated interpretation ids and summaries, and an explicit statement that this is unresolved and the DM must not assert a canonical answer or silently pick one. For each ambiguity WITH an active ruling, carry the ruling's prose beside the ambiguity rather than replacing or hiding the source material.
- Use listActiveRulingsForAmbiguitiesAtPosition from eshyra-jhpt.2 for the resolved/unresolved determination. Never write a winner or default back into the pack; assert pack immutability in a test.

TESTS
Prospective and effective-turn filtering (a rule effective later is absent now, present at/after its position); superseded and revoked rules absent at positions after the change and present before; deterministic ordering; A1 association data present; all three ambiguities surfaced unresolved with interpretations and no preferred winner; an ambiguity with an active ruling carries both ruling and source; pack bytes unchanged; position idempotency per part 1.

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root, BEFORE committing (it rewrites files).
